claims.title: Canaanite city-states of the Bronze Age
claims.summary: Walled Canaanite towns flourished across the southern Levant, trading with Egypt and Mesopotamia and forming the region's earliest urban civilisation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-3000bce-canaanite-city-states-of-the-bronze-age, claim TL:PSE:event:3000bce:canaanite-city-states-of-the-bronze-age, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Arrival of the Philistines
claims.summary: The Philistines settled the southern coastal plain, founding cities such as Gaza, Ashkelon, and Ashdod; their name would later give the land the name 'Palestine'.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-1175bce-arrival-of-the-philistines, claim TL:PSE:event:1175bce:arrival-of-the-philistines, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Babylonian conquest of Jerusalem
claims.summary: Neo-Babylonian forces under Nebuchadnezzar II captured Jerusalem and destroyed the First Temple, deporting much of the population to Babylon.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-586bce-babylonian-conquest-of-jerusalem, claim TL:PSE:event:586bce:babylonian-conquest-of-jerusalem, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Persian rule under the Achaemenids
claims.summary: Cyrus the Great conquered Babylon and incorporated the region into the Persian Empire, permitting exiled communities to return.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-539bce-persian-rule-under-the-achaemenids, claim TL:PSE:event:539bce:persian-rule-under-the-achaemenids, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hellenistic conquest
claims.summary: Alexander the Great's conquest brought the region into the Hellenistic world of the Ptolemaic and Seleucid kingdoms.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-332bce-hellenistic-conquest, claim TL:PSE:event:332bce:hellenistic-conquest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Roman conquest
claims.summary: The Roman general Pompey took Jerusalem, bringing the region under Roman authority as the province of Judaea.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-63bce-roman-conquest, claim TL:PSE:event:63bce:roman-conquest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Province renamed Syria Palaestina
claims.summary: After crushing the Bar Kokhba revolt, the emperor Hadrian renamed the province Syria Palaestina, formalising the name 'Palestine' in Roman administration.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-135-province-renamed-syria-palaestina, claim TL:PSE:event:135:province-renamed-syria-palaestina, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: A Christian holy land
claims.summary: Following Constantine's conversion, Palestine became a centre of Christian pilgrimage; churches were built over sites venerated as those of Jesus's life, death, and resurrection.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-326-a-christian-holy-land, claim TL:PSE:event:326:a-christian-holy-land, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Arab Muslim conquest of Jerusalem
claims.summary: Jerusalem surrendered to the caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab, beginning nearly a millennium of predominantly Islamic rule and the region's gradual Arabisation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-638-arab-muslim-conquest-of-jerusalem, claim TL:PSE:event:638:arab-muslim-conquest-of-jerusalem, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Building of the Dome of the Rock
claims.summary: The Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik built the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, an early masterpiece of Islamic architecture on the Haram al-Sharif.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-691-building-of-the-dome-of-the-rock, claim TL:PSE:event:691:building-of-the-dome-of-the-rock, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Crusaders capture Jerusalem
claims.summary: The First Crusade seized Jerusalem and founded the Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem, holding the city until 1187.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-1099-crusaders-capture-jerusalem, claim TL:PSE:event:1099:crusaders-capture-jerusalem, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Saladin retakes Jerusalem
claims.summary: Saladin, founder of the Ayyubid dynasty, defeated the Crusaders and recaptured Jerusalem, largely ending Crusader rule over the city.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-1187-saladin-retakes-jerusalem, claim TL:PSE:event:1187:saladin-retakes-jerusalem, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mamluk rule established
claims.summary: The Mamluk sultanate of Egypt expelled the last Crusaders from the Levant and governed Palestine until the Ottoman conquest.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-1291-mamluk-rule-established, claim TL:PSE:event:1291:mamluk-rule-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ottoman conquest
claims.summary: Sultan Selim I defeated the Mamluks and incorporated Palestine into the Ottoman Empire, beginning four centuries of Ottoman rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-1517-ottoman-conquest, claim TL:PSE:event:1517:ottoman-conquest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First waves of Zionist immigration
claims.summary: From the 1880s organised Jewish immigration (the aliyot) began establishing agricultural colonies in Ottoman Palestine, driven by persecution in Europe and an emerging national idea.

sources.label: Origins and Evolution of the Palestine Problem, Part I (1917-1947)

claims.title: First Zionist Congress
claims.summary: Theodor Herzl convened the First Zionist Congress in Basel, founding the World Zionist Organization and adopting the aim of a Jewish national home in Palestine.

sources.label: Origins and Evolution of the Palestine Problem, Part I (1917-1947)

claims.title: Balfour Declaration
claims.summary: Britain declared its support for a Jewish national home in Palestine while affirming the rights of the existing, overwhelmingly Arab, non-Jewish communities.

sources.label: Origins and Evolution of the Palestine Problem, Part I (1917-1947)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-1917-balfour-declaration, claim TL:PSE:event:1917:balfour-declaration, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: British Mandate for Palestine
claims.summary: The League of Nations entrusted Britain with governing Palestine; the Mandate incorporated the Balfour Declaration's commitment to a Jewish national home.

sources.label: Origins and Evolution of the Palestine Problem, Part I (1917-1947)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-1922-british-mandate-for-palestine, claim TL:PSE:event:1922:british-mandate-for-palestine, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Arab Revolt in Palestine
claims.summary: A sustained Palestinian Arab uprising against British rule and Zionist immigration was suppressed with great severity, leaving Palestinian society weakened.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-1936-arab-revolt-in-palestine, claim TL:PSE:event:1936:arab-revolt-in-palestine, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: UN Partition Plan (Resolution 181)
claims.summary: The UN General Assembly recommended partition into Jewish and Arab states with Jerusalem internationalised; accepted by Zionist leaders and rejected by Palestinian and Arab leaders.

sources.label: General Assembly Resolution 181 (II): Future Government of Palestine

claims.title: The Nakba
claims.summary: During the war surrounding Israel's establishment, around 700,000 Palestinians were expelled or fled and, per UN figures, more than 500 villages were depopulated and destroyed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-1948-the-nakba, claim TL:PSE:event:1948:the-nakba, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the PLO
claims.summary: The Palestine Liberation Organization was established as the umbrella body of the Palestinian national movement, later led by Yasser Arafat.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-1964-founding-of-the-plo, claim TL:PSE:event:1964:founding-of-the-plo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Israeli occupation of the West Bank and Gaza
claims.summary: In the Six-Day War Israel captured the West Bank, East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip, placing most Palestinians under a military occupation that endures.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-1967-israeli-occupation-of-the-west-bank-and-gaza, claim TL:PSE:event:1967:israeli-occupation-of-the-west-bank-and-gaza, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First Intifada
claims.summary: A sustained popular uprising against the Israeli occupation of the West Bank and Gaza brought the Palestinian cause to renewed international attention.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-1987-first-intifada, claim TL:PSE:event:1987:first-intifada, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Declaration of the State of Palestine
claims.summary: The Palestinian National Council in Algiers, chaired by Yasser Arafat, proclaimed the independent State of Palestine with Jerusalem as its capital.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-1988-declaration-of-the-state-of-palestine, claim TL:PSE:event:1988:declaration-of-the-state-of-palestine, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Oslo Accords
claims.summary: Israel and the PLO exchanged mutual recognition and agreed a framework for Palestinian interim self-government, creating the Palestinian Authority.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-1993-oslo-accords, claim TL:PSE:event:1993:oslo-accords, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Second Intifada
claims.summary: A second Palestinian uprising brought years of violence and Israeli military operations, ending the optimism of the Oslo era.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-2000-second-intifada, claim TL:PSE:event:2000:second-intifada, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Blockade of the Gaza Strip
claims.summary: After Hamas took control of Gaza, Israel and Egypt imposed a blockade restricting the movement of people and goods, with severe humanitarian consequences.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Palestine: An ancient and contested land at the crossroads of three continents and three faiths, whose people declared an independent state in 1988 and whose modern history is defined by dispossession and the struggle for self-determination.", terralore.co/country/PSE/chronicle#ev-2007-blockade-of-the-gaza-strip, claim TL:PSE:event:2007:blockade-of-the-gaza-strip, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: UN recognition as non-member observer state
claims.summary: The UN General Assembly, by resolution 67/19, recognised the State of Palestine as a non-member observer state by 138 votes to 9 with 41 abstentions.

sources.label: General Assembly Resolution 67/19: Status of Palestine in the United Nations

claims.title: The Gaza war
claims.summary: After a Hamas-led attack on southern Israel killed about 1,200 people, Israel launched a massive campaign in Gaza; by Gaza Health Ministry figures cited by the UN, tens of thousands of Palestinians, mostly women and children, have been killed.

sources.label: Israel has committed genocide in the Gaza Strip, UN Commission finds

claims.title: ICJ provisional-measures order in South Africa v. Israel
claims.summary: The International Court of Justice found at least some rights under the Genocide Convention plausible and a real and imminent risk to them, ordering Israel to prevent genocidal acts; the case remains under adjudication.

sources.label: Summary of the Order of 26 January 2024 (South Africa v. Israel)
Application of the Genocide Convention in the Gaza Strip (South Africa v. Israel) - case overview

claims.title: UN Special Rapporteur's 'Anatomy of a Genocide'
claims.summary: UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese reported reasonable grounds to believe genocide was being committed against Palestinians in Gaza (A/HRC/55/73).

claims.title: Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch findings
claims.summary: Amnesty International (5 December) concluded Israel was committing genocide; Human Rights Watch (19 December) found acts of genocide and the crime against humanity of extermination.

claims.summary: The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory concluded that Israel had committed genocide in the Gaza Strip; Israel rejected the findings.

sources.label: Israel has committed genocide in the Gaza Strip, UN Commission finds
